Four birth records circulate. Eight of his nine planets are identical in all of them.

19 JUN 1970 · NEW DELHI

TL;DR

One planet in dispute. Eight that aren't.

Most celebrity kundli pages have one birth time and a lot of confidence. Rahul Gandhi's kundli has four published records — and running all of them through our engine turns out to be the most interesting thing on this page.
Three records put him on the afternoon of 19 June 1970 (14:28, 14:31, 14:45). A fourth, on India's largest kundli site, puts him on the previous evening entirely. We computed the birth chart at every one of them.

The result: eight of the nine grahas land in exactly the same sign no matter which record you use. Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rahu and Ketu don't move. Only the Moon does — and that single disagreement is what stops this page making any house-level claim about him.

Mithuna · Gemini
Sun at 4°13′ Gemini, in Mrigashira nakshatra. Identical on every published record.

The Moon
Sagittarius / Mula on the 19 June records; Scorpio / Jyeshtha on the 18 June one. So: no lagna, no houses, no dated dashas.
The public record

Fifty-six years, on the record

A milestone rail, not a scoreboard. Every point below is a matter of public record — dates of birth, education, election and office. We are deliberately not plotting anything like "popularity", and nothing here is a claim that the chart caused, predicted or explains any of it.

1970–2003 · BEFORE POLITICS

Delhi, Dehradun, Florida, Cambridge

33 years of not being in electoral politics
  • Born 19 June 1970 at Holy Family Hospital, Delhi. Schooled at St. Columba's in Delhi and briefly at The Doon School, Dehradun (1981–83), then St. Stephen's College.
  • Completed his degree at Rollins College, Florida in 1994, and an MPhil in Development Studies at Trinity College, Cambridge in 1995.
  • He spent the rest of the 1990s and early 2000s outside elected office.

The entry, at 33

  • He announced his entry into electoral politics in March 2004, ahead of the 14th general election, and was elected MP for Amethi in Uttar Pradesh.
  • He held the Amethi seat across the 2004, 2009 and 2014 elections — fifteen years in the same constituency.
  • He was appointed a General Secretary of the Indian National Congress in 2007.

136 days Kanyakumari to Srinagar
  • The Bharat Jodo Yatra ran from 7 September 2022 to 30 January 2023, from Kanyakumari to Srinagar, covering roughly 3,500–4,000 km.
  • The Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra followed from 14 January to March 2024, from Manipur to Mumbai, largely by bus with walking stretches, across 14 states.

  • Elected MP for Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh, in 2024 — his fifth term in the Lok Sabha.
  • Named Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha in June 2024. The post had sat vacant for ten years, because no single opposition party had cleared the required share of seats.

Straight answers

The three things people actually search

🕰️ "What is Rahul Gandhi's birth time?"
What's published

Four different records circulate. Astrodienst's Astro-Databank carries 19 June 1970, 14:28, New Delhi — the most-cited one. A newspaper horoscope column uses 14:31. Another site uses 14:45. India's largest kundli site publishes something else entirely: 18 June 1970, 21:52, citing a printed collection.

That fourth record disagrees with his documented date of birth, which every biography and Parliament record puts on 19 June 1970.

What we computed

We ran the chart at all four. The 14:28 / 14:31 / 14:45 group is astrologically indistinguishable — same signs, same nakshatras, same padas, and the ascendant is in Libra for all three (Libra rises from 14:19 to 16:39 IST that day).

The 18 June record puts the ascendant in Capricorn and the Moon in a different nakshatra. Because we can't adjudicate between a printed collection and a databank, we simply don't build anything on the ascendant. Sign-level only.

💍 "Is Rahul Gandhi manglik?"
The honest answer

We won't give you a verdict, and any site that does is guessing. Mangal dosha is a house-level judgement — it asks which house Mars occupies counted from the ascendant, and the ascendant needs a birth minute we don't have agreement on.

What we can say

Mars is in Gemini, at 17°48′, in Ardra nakshatra — and that is fixed on every published record. It is also combust: only 13°35′ from the Sun, close enough that traditional texts treat it as burnt.

Counted from the Moon rather than the ascendant, the classical rule does flag Mars — but the same texts cancel it, because Jupiter aspects Mars here. That's a sign-level observation, not a verdict, and it is the most we can honestly offer without the minute.

🗳️ "What does his horoscope say about 2029?"
What astrologers say

It's one of the most-searched things about his chart, and a steady stream of astrologers, YouTube channels and Hindi dailies publish "raj yoga" and "PM yog" readings about it — for him and for every other major politician in the country.

What we compute — and won't

AxtroShastra does not publish election predictions. Not for him, not for anyone. An election is decided by tens of millions of people, and a birth chart is not a polling model.

There is a technical reason too. Any dated forecast rides on the Vimshottari dasha, and the dasha dates here depend on the exact minute of birth. Across the four published records the dasha sequence doesn't just shift — it starts on a different planet. Anyone quoting you a dated period for 2029 has quietly picked one record and not told you.

Being straight with you: everything in the left-hand columns is public record. Everything in the right-hand columns is either something our engine computed, or a note about what traditional astrology would look at — offered for interest and education. None of it is a claim about this person's motives, decisions or future, and none of it is a political statement.
Two arcs

Two stretches that are documented

🎓 → 🗳️  Thirty-three years, then a constituency

  • He finished an MPhil at Cambridge in 1995 and spent the following years outside elected politics.
  • He announced he would contest in March 2004, at 33, and was elected MP for Amethi that year.
  • He has been returned to the Lok Sabha at every general election since — Amethi in 2004, 2009 and 2014, Wayanad in 2019, Rae Bareli in 2024.

🔭 The chart bit: nothing dated, because we can't date anything here. What we can say is that the entry happened during the second mahadasha in his sequence on the 19 June records — and we're telling you the lord's name, not a date, precisely because the date moves with the record.

👣 → 🏛️  About 10,000 kilometres, then a front bench

  • Between September 2022 and March 2024 he covered the length of the country twice over — Kanyakumari to Srinagar on foot, then Manipur to Mumbai.
  • In June 2024 he was named Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, a post that had been vacant since 2014.
  • Both facts are drawn from the parliamentary and public record, not from any interpretation.

🔭 The chart bit: a debilitated Saturn is the classical signature for results that arrive late and are paid for in distance covered rather than doors opened. Read that as a description of a placement, not as an explanation of an outcome.

One note on his family, stated once. His grandmother, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, was assassinated in 1984, when he was fourteen; his father, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, was assassinated in 1991, when he was twenty. These are matters of public record and we state them here as biography, briefly, because a page about his life that silently omitted them would be dishonest. They appear nowhere else on this page. No placement, dasha or yoga on this page is offered as a cause, a prediction or an explanation of them — we consider that line one nobody should cross, and we don't.
The placements

Four planets. What the sky wrote.

All four of these are computed by our engine, and all four are identical on every published birth record — which is exactly why we're willing to write about them.

♄
SATURN · ARIES
DEBILITATED
Saturn · 24°28′ Aries · Bharani · weakest spot

The patience planet, in its worst sign

  • Saturn runs endurance, structure, delay and the long unglamorous middle of things. In Aries — the sign of the immediate, impatient start — it sits in its classical debilitation.
  • This is the single clearly weak placement in the whole chart. Nothing else here is debilitated, and nothing else is exalted either.
  • The traditional reading is not "fails" — it's that the Saturn things (waiting, grinding, structural work) never feel natural and have to be done the hard way, deliberately.
  • It holds at every published birth time, because Saturn moves roughly one degree a month.

Photo: at the conclusion of the Bharat Jodo Yatra, Srinagar, January 2023.

♂
MARS · GEMINI
COMBUST
Mars · 17°48′ Gemini · Ardra · combust

The drive planet, standing too close to the Sun

  • Mars is the planet of drive, confrontation and physical push. Here it sits in Gemini — an air sign of talk and argument rather than force.
  • It is also combust: 13°35′ from the Sun, inside the traditional burning range, which classical texts read as the planet's own character being drowned out by the Sun's.
  • Combust Mars is usually read as force that comes out as words and positions rather than as the blunt article — and as a temper that is easier to see than to locate.
  • Mars and the Sun sit in the same sign on all four records, so the combustion is not in dispute.

Photo: public address, Shillong, January 2018.

♃
JUPITER · LIBRA
RETROGRADE
Jupiter · 2°39′ Libra · Chitra · retrograde

The teacher planet, running backwards

  • Jupiter governs teaching, counsel, doctrine and the impulse to explain. It sits in Libra, the sign of balance and negotiation, and it is retrograde.
  • A retrograde Jupiter is traditionally read as wisdom that arrives by revisiting rather than by receiving — the person who keeps going back over the same argument until it comes out right, rather than accepting the received version.
  • It is also the closest planet in this chart to the disputed ascendant degree — under the 19 June records it is within a degree of the rising point. We're flagging that as an interesting near-miss, not building a reading on it, because the ascendant isn't settled.
  • Jupiter takes about a year per sign, so this too is fixed regardless of the minute.

Photo: address at Stanford University, 2023.

☾
MOON · DISPUTED
SAG or SCO
Moon · the one placement nobody agrees on

The planet that decides the rest — and it's contested

  • On the three 19 June records the Moon is at 2°15′ Sagittarius, in Mula nakshatra, first pada — the "root" star, ruled by Ketu.
  • On the 18 June record it is in Scorpio, in Jyeshtha, and debilitated. Same person, entirely different emotional signature.
  • This matters more than any other single disagreement, because the Moon's nakshatra is what sets the whole Vimshottari dasha clock. Mula starts the sequence at Ketu. Jyeshtha starts it at Mercury. Everything downstream shifts.
  • So we publish the mahadasha order for the majority record and no dates at all. A dated timeline here would be a guess wearing a lab coat.

Photo: official PIB portrait, New Delhi, November 2025.

Astrology, explained properly

Astrology, but make it make sense

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

A kundli is a map of where the nine grahas sat, as seen from your birthplace, at the moment you were born. Vedic astrology uses the sidereal zodiac — measured against the actual stars — which is why the Vedic sun sign is usually one behind the Western one. His is Gemini in both here, but that's a coincidence of degree, not a rule.

His Sun sits at 4°13′ Gemini. Western astrology, measuring from the equinox instead, would put it near 27° Gemini. Same sky, different ruler.
LESSON 02

The planets, and what each one runs

Nine grahas, nine departments. This is the whole vocabulary you need to read the table above.

GrahaRunsIn his chart
☉ Sunauthority, self, the fatherGemini
☾ Moonmind, mood, the motherdisputed
♂ Marsdrive, conflict, courageGemini, combust
☿ Mercuryspeech, analysis, tradeTaurus
♃ Jupitercounsel, doctrine, teachingLibra, retrograde
♀ Venuscharm, comfort, partnershipCancer
♄ Saturnendurance, delay, structureAries, debilitated
☊ Rahuhunger, reach, obsessionAquarius
☋ Ketudetachment, letting goLeo
LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it works easily (exalted, own sign) and one where it works worst (debilitated). It's not good or bad — it's whether the planet gets to be itself or has to work against the grain.

Saturn is debilitated in Aries. Nothing else in his chart is either debilitated or exalted, which makes that one placement the loudest thing in it.
LESSON 04

Combustion — standing too close to the boss

When a planet sits within a few degrees of the Sun, classical texts call it combust — burnt, its own signal drowned out by a much louder one. Mars is combust here.

Mars is 13°35′ from the Sun. For Mars the traditional burning range is about 17°, so it falls inside it.
LESSON 05

Dashas — why timing is normally the whole game

The Vimshottari dasha system splits a life into planetary periods running in a fixed order, each a fixed number of years. Which planet you start on, and how far into it you are born, is set by exactly one thing: the precise position of the Moon at birth.

On the 19 June records the Moon is in Mula, so the sequence opens with Ketu. On the 18 June record it's in Jyeshtha, so it opens with Mercury instead. Same life, two different clocks.
LESSON 06

The boundary that decides everything above

We swept the whole of 19 June 1970 at ten-minute steps. The Moon crosses from Jyeshtha into Mula at 10:45 IST that morning — so a birth before lunch and a birth after it produce different dasha sequences from the same date.

All three afternoon records sit more than three and a half hours clear of that boundary, which is why they agree with each other completely. The fourth record is on a different day altogether.
LESSON 07

What we genuinely can't tell you

The rising sign (lagna) changes roughly every two hours, and the twelve houses hang off it. Libra rises over New Delhi from 14:19 to 16:39 IST on 19 June 1970 — so all three afternoon records land in Libra, nine minutes or more clear of the cusp. That is real.

But the fourth record, on 18 June, gives Capricorn. Because we can't referee between them, we don't publish a lagna reading, a house analysis, a marriage-house claim or a manglik verdict. Anything you read elsewhere that does has quietly chosen one record for you.

Being able to compute something is not the same as being entitled to publish it.
LESSON 08

And one thing we won't do at all

We don't publish election forecasts from birth charts — his or anyone else's — and we don't read a chart as an endorsement or a criticism of a living politician. Where astrologers publicly discuss his chart, we'll tell you that they do; we won't join in.

A chart describes a set of placements. It does not describe an electorate.

Quick answers

What people ask about his kundli

FAQ 01

What is Rahul Gandhi's birth time?

There is no single settled answer. Astrodienst's Astro-Databank records 14:28 on 19 June 1970 in New Delhi, and that is the most widely reproduced figure; 14:31 and 14:45 also appear in print. Separately, AstroSage publishes 21:52 on 18 June 1970, citing a printed collection — a record that disagrees with his documented date of birth. We treat the birth time as disputed and publish only what survives all four.

FAQ 02

What is Rahul Gandhi's zodiac sign and nakshatra?

His Vedic (sidereal) sun sign is Gemini — Sun at 4°13′ Gemini in Mrigashira nakshatra — and that is identical on every published birth record. His Western sun sign is also Gemini. The Moon sign and birth nakshatra are the disputed part: Sagittarius / Mula on the 19 June records, Scorpio / Jyeshtha on the 18 June one. If someone quotes you one of those as settled fact, they've picked a record without telling you.

FAQ 03

Is Rahul Gandhi manglik?

We don't publish a verdict, because an honest one isn't available. Mangal dosha is judged from the ascendant, and the ascendant depends on a birth minute that four sources disagree about. What we can say from the birth date alone: Mars is in Gemini at 17°48′ and is combust. Counted from the Moon, the classical rule does raise the flag — and the same classical texts then cancel it, because Jupiter aspects Mars. That's the full honest answer at sign level.

FAQ 04

What does his horoscope say about 2029?

Nothing that we will publish. AxtroShastra does not issue election predictions from anyone's birth chart, and this page takes no position for or against any party or candidate. There's a technical reason as well as an editorial one: every dated dasha forecast depends on the exact birth minute, and across the four published records his dasha sequence begins on a different planet. So we publish the mahadasha order and no dates at all.

Method. Every placement, degree, nakshatra and boundary time on this page was computed with the Swiss Ephemeris using the Lahiri ayanamsa — the same engine behind every AxtroShastra report — and nothing was copied from another astrology site. We ran the chart at all four published birth records and at ten-minute steps across the whole of 19 June 1970. Because those records disagree on the Moon and therefore on the ascendant, this page carries no lagna, no house analysis, no manglik verdict and no dated dasha periods. The mahadasha order is published; the dates are not.

Birth-time status. Disputed. Astro-Databank: 19 Jun 1970, 14:28, New Delhi. Also published: 14:31 and 14:45 the same afternoon, and 18 Jun 1970 21:52 from a separate printed source. Eight of the nine grahas are unaffected; the Moon is not.
